source.title: Task-Specific Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Monosemantic Neuronal Activations
source.authors: Da Ma; Gonghu Shang; Zhi Chen; Libo Qin; Yijie Luo; Lei Pan; Shuai Fan; Lu Chen; Kai Yu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses the premise that SAE features are monosemantic to build a data-selection method. Its reported outcomes concern data-selection and downstream task performance, not how many neurons have a single interpretable job or whether explanations predict activations.
record.gate_note: The paper compares data selection based on polysemantic and SAE-derived monosemantic activations, and describes activation-profile plots. These results do not measure the claim versions' neuron-job shares, explanation fidelity, or attribution-graph sufficiency. The performance comparison is recorded as a related finding, not as evidence for a claim version.
record.test_reason: The study assumes raw neurons are polysemantic and SAE features monosemantic, and uses SAE activations as a tool for instruction-tuning data selection. It reports only its method's downstream performance (MMLU, BBH, TydiQA, etc.) and a qualitative activation-profile plot. It does not measure what share of neurons have one job, test explanations against activations, or build attribution graphs. Its stance runs against the claim's premise, but only as an assumption, not a measured result.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SAE-derived monosemantic activations, compared using generalized Jaccard similarity, give better and more stable task-specific data selection than baselines across models and tasks. They assume neuron polysemanticity, citing prior work, rather than measuring it.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SAE-derived activations to select instruction-tuning data and evaluates downstream task performance; it does not audit neuron explanations or predict activations on held-out examples.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported data-selection performance varies with layer choice, sparsity parameter K, and similarity metric; the authors report stronger results for deeper layers, larger tested K values, and Jaccard similarity.

fits_no_version.finding: Data selected using SAE activations gives slightly higher downstream scores than selection using top-K gated-MLP neuron activations or raw hidden states (Table 8, average 67.20 vs 65.95 vs 65.19).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In task-specific data selection, SAE feature activations give better downstream performance than raw neuron activations.

fits_no_version.finding: In a visual plot, raw neuron activations overlap across math and code samples, while SAE features separate by task (Figure 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features are more task-specific than raw MLP neurons at the level of a task (math vs code).

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code will be released but gives no release URL.
record.problems: The study does not test neuron-job interpretations or their predictive fidelity. The activation-profile evidence is a visual comparison, and Table 8 does not state the backbone model or report uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported results concern general data-selection performance, curation, or sensitivity to data-selection settings rather than neuron interpretability or the claim versions, so they were not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or their job shares.
No neuron-job shares in any model or at any scale.
No analysis of InceptionV1 or of canonical polysemantic neurons.
No interpretable-neuron shares and no test of architecture or tools as their cause.
No attribution graphs or circuit analysis.
No test of whether explanations predict where neurons fire.
No automated simulation scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation (uses_without_test) and tranche (T4) are correct. Polysemanticity of raw neurons is a premise backed by a cited example (citations and HTTP requests), not a measured share. The 'polysemantic' baseline is top-K gated-MLP activations (Appendix B.3), so the Table 8 gap mixes representation type with the SAE tool. It is not evidence on any version.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or estimates of single-job, two-job, or not-understood shares.
No comparison of neuron-job shares across models, architectures, or scale.
No analysis of InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons or recursive generalization.
No estimate of interpretable-neuron shares or test of architecture, regularization, tools, or model capacity as their cause.
No attribution graphs or test of whether model neurons suffice as circuit units.
No test of explanations against activations on examples separate from those used to write the explanations.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by predicting activations on new text.
